subject.title: Add plan-first Claw status and remove

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this core Claws lifecycle only after status and remove become one authoritative inventory, consent, deletion, recovery, and audit contract across agent, session, file, package, MCP, and cron owners?
rationale: The remaining blockers are not only mechanical defects: the open RFC and latest human feedback require a maintainer choice about the permanent destructive lifecycle, persistence, recovery, and tombstone boundary.

options.title: Revise the full lifecycle
options.body: Require this stack to implement authoritative orphan-aware inventory, complete consent, canonical deletion, serialized ownership, and a redacted tombstone before merge.

options.title: Land status only
options.body: Keep read-only inventory in this slice and defer destructive removal until the complete owner and recovery contract is approved.

options.title: Pause the stack
options.body: Leave the series open without landing until maintainers choose a different lifecycle or persistence boundary.

recommendation.title: Revise the full lifecycle
recommendation.body: Require this stack to implement authoritative orphan-aware inventory, complete consent, canonical deletion, serialized ownership, and a redacted tombstone before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their current-main history spans the shared SQLite, config-mutation, and filesystem-safety boundaries that must define this cross-owner contract.
